assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept, production game environment asset.
Reference image role: approved style and world-layout reference A, pixel adventure. Create ONLY the game-world island art as an asset for a playable 2.5D web game named Volodymyr's Planet.
Preserve reference's premium handcrafted isometric pixel art, mossy grass, warm cream/copper buildings, slate rock strata, pine trees and bright glacial blue ice. Fixed orthographic/isometric three-quarter camera. Planar walkable ground on a thick floating island, not a spherical world.
CRITICAL: NO text anywhere. NO title, NO logos, NO UI, NO interface frame, NO panels, NO labels, NO key hints, NO color swatches, NO character studies. NO player characters or people on the map. This is a clean environment layer.
Transparent background beyond island and a few small floating stone fragments; real alpha, no checkerboard. Entire island fully visible with generous 5% margins, LANDSCAPE canvas 1536x1024 or equivalent 3:2 ratio. Island has broad oval-ish upper surface, visible geological strata bottom edge tapering into rock. Main island about 90% of canvas width and 85% height.
Match geography: upper-left quadrant cream radar station with copper trim, dish antenna and small solar panel; upper-right quadrant glacial ice field with frozen pool and tiny instrument station; lower-left woodland library cabin with green roof and visible books, lower-right canvas exploration camp with small campfire and map table.
Very important for gameplay: wide unobstructed tan dirt footpaths in a connected crossroads, winding from radar station doorstep to center, center to front of glacial station, center to library doorstep, center to campsite. Keep central crossroads and these paths entirely clear of stones/trees/props, with broad walkable grassy shoulders. Buildings off the paths, stairs end on paths. Do not place trees on the central crossroads. No bridges or isolated unconnected destinations. Environment detailed at the edges but navigation visually obvious. Sparse flower patches, occasional small rocks away from trails. No dramatic perspective, no blur, no depth-of-field, no photorealism. Controlled deliberate pixel edges and warm nuanced sprite shading matching reference. Render a single coherent gorgeous game-level asset, not a design board.

Use case: stylized-concept, production pixel-art sprite sheet.
Reference image role: style and character reference from approved A / pixel adventure design. Create a clean transparent sprite sheet of ONLY the little white-hooded explorer character shown in reference (cream hooded parka, brown hair, orange/russet field backpack, navy pants, brown boots, handheld blue-tipped probe). Original charming pixel RPG character, crisp consistent pixel grid, dark ink outlines, subtle warm shading.
EXACT LAYOUT: square 1024x1024 canvas. Exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, exactly 16 sprites, no gaps between the logical 256x256 cells. Each sprite centered horizontally in its own cell with feet baseline 225 pixels down inside the cell. Every sprite same apparent scale and same proportions, about 175px tall within its 256px cell, transparent margins. Do not draw cell borders or labels. Do not crop any sprite.
Rows are directions: row1 facing SOUTH toward viewer; row2 facing WEST to viewer's left; row3 facing EAST to viewer's right; row4 facing NORTH away from viewer showing orange backpack.
Columns are a simple 4-frame walk loop: col1 neutral standing; col2 left-foot step and opposite arm; col3 neutral passing pose; col4 right-foot step and opposite arm. Small controlled variations suitable for a walking loop. No weapons; handheld geological probe only.
Flat orthographic game sprite view, three-quarter top-down compatible with an isometric map. All 16 characters identical identity and outfit. No extra heads, no detached accessories, no props, no environment, no ground, no cast shadow, no text, no watermark. TRUE transparent alpha background, not white, not checkerboard. Keep 4x4 alignment and constant feet baseline exact so software can draw each 256x256 frame directly.
